reasons: **Heat is close to the limit, but under it.** On the hottest stretch, body temperatures are expected to reach about 37.9 °C. The safe limit is 38.0 °C, so at the tightest point we're less than a tenth of a degree from it. Watch the crew closely and be ready to call extra breaks if conditions get worse than forecast.

**We're getting a bit over half the work done, with the most important jobs first.** This plan finishes about 60% of the work, weighted toward the highest-priority tasks. Another option gets 62% done, but it runs workers slightly hotter (about 37.92 °C). A third option gets the same 60% but runs even hotter (about 37.96 °C), so this plan is the safer way to get that amount done.

**Kofi is kept off the heaviest work in the heat.** He's new and his body hasn't adjusted to working in high heat yet. So he won't be given very heavy tasks during the hottest periods, even if it means others pick up more or some work waits.
